summary: Navajo Nation ground-house lookout on a black rock pinnacle above Canyon de Chelly, built 1936, still a key detection station per NHLR; registered 2002.

facts.design: Wood ground house reached by metal steps up a black rock pinnacle

staffing.status: described as a key detection station; no current staffing record found

facts.agency: Navajo Indian Reservation (administering); Bureau of Indian Affairs (cooperator)

events.note: Ground house constructed at the Navajo Reservation site
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register July 20, 2002

evidence.supports: Wood ground house with metal steps on a black rock pinnacle, overlooking the north end of Canyon de Chelly
evidence.quote: Overlooking the north end of Canyon De Chelly National Monument, Black Pinnacle Lookout is a unique wood ground house reached by a series of metal steps atop on a black rock pinnacle

evidence.supports: Constructed in 1936 and remains a key detection station
evidence.quote: The Navajo Reservation site was constructed in 1936 and remains a key detection station.

evidence.supports: Administered by the Navajo Indian Reservation, with the Bureau of Indian Affairs as cooperator
evidence.quote: Administered by Navajo Indian Reservation Cooperators Bureau of Indian Affairs

evidence.supports: Location on the Navajo Indian Reservation in Apache County
Listed as a standing ground lookout
evidence.quote: Black Pinnacle Apache 36.25258 -109.15706 Ground Standing NHLR US 436, AZ 32

corrections.proposed: no access level (not supported by any source read)
corrections.why: NHLR names the administering Navajo Indian Reservation and the BIA cooperator but gives no visiting rule, and no page read says permission is required.

notes_for_editor: The history rests on one NHLR entry. No staffing, access or rental source was found, and the brief's 'permission' access level is not supported by any page read, so removal is proposed. The search budget was used up, so Navajo Nation or BIA records were not checked.
